_comment: Which pack machine crafts a Factorio recipe category (ADR-0026's conversion input).
Routing is on a recipe's FIRST category. Factorio 2.x gives a recipe a list, and the
extra entries are the DLC machines that may also craft it -- `transport-belt` is
["crafting", "metallurgy"] because Vulcanus's foundry exists, not because a belt is a
metallurgy recipe. Routing on anything but the first entry would hand Terra's recipes to
machines this map does not build.
A `!` prefix means the category is deliberately not routed: the converter emits nothing
and says why. It is not the same as a category missing from this file, which is a hard
failure -- a new Factorio version adding a category must not silently drop its recipes.

A `recipe_type` of null is a machine that is not registered yet, and `blocked_by` names the ticket that registers it. The recipe converter, in the private corpus repository, reads both, so the converter holds no table of its own. A null with no `blocked_by` is a machine nobody has ticketed.
A machine's `category` replaces the Factorio category its recipes carry, for a Factorio category Craftworks does not have; `recipe_dir` replaces its recipe type's path in the recipe id.

assembling.note: Factorio's Assembling Machine 1/2/3, which are Craftworks' Assemblers (ADR-0118), and the Personal Assembler. Factorio's Chemical Plant and Oil Refinery have no machine of their own: their recipes run on Assembler 2 and 3 (ADR-0125). One type across the five Factorio categories, each recipe carrying its `category` and `hand_craftable`: the converter sets the flag for a first category of `crafting`, and Craftworks' Personal Assembler plans only a hand-craftable recipe. Recipe ids stay `factoryworks:assembling/<name>`.

chemistry.note: Factorio's Chemical Plant recipes, on Craftworks' Assembler 2 and 3: Craftworks has no Chemical Plant and no `chemistry` category (Craftworks ADR-0018), so they load as `crafting-with-fluid` (ADR-0125). They stay under `chemistry/` so their ids and research unlocks do not move.

oil_processing.note: Factorio's Oil Refinery recipes, on Craftworks' Assembler 2 and 3: Craftworks has no Oil Refinery and no `oil-processing` category (Craftworks ADR-0018), so they load as `crafting-with-fluid` (ADR-0125). They stay under `oil_processing/` so their ids and research unlocks do not move.

smelting.note: Plates and stone brick, on the pack's own `factoryworks:smelting` (#155) and on nothing else. The three furnace tiers are `factoryworks_core` blocks (Stone, Steel, Electric), which is why `subgroup-owner.json` reads `pack:smelting`. ADR-0032 deleted ADR-0017's Ore processing row -- ore is 1:1, so smelting rides nothing and is the whole of ore-to-plate. The type carries a count on the ingredient, which is what lets `steel-plate` (5 plates to 1) and `stone-brick` (2 stone to 1, ADR-0046) be expressed at all; vanilla `minecraft:smelting` can express neither, and is not read alongside it because ADR-0034's sweep leaves it with no live recipe.

centrifuge.note: ADR-0033. Uranium processing and nuclear fuel reprocessing; Kovarex when the post-launch map reaches it. #135 registers it, and the id will be `gtceu:`.

rocket_silo.note: The Rocket Part. #29 and #41 settle what a launch consumes; the silo is GCyR's.
